discovery: Dynamical mean-field theory of strongly correlated electron systems

nominees.name: Antoine Georges
nominees.affiliation: Collège de France, Paris; Flatiron Institute, New York; University of Geneva

subfield: Condensed matter theory: strongly correlated electrons
motivation: Vollhardt (with Metzner) showed that lattice fermion models acquire a nontrivial, exactly solvable limit in infinite dimensions. Georges and Kotliar then mapped this limit onto a self-consistent quantum impurity problem, creating dynamical mean-field theory (DMFT). DMFT gave the first controlled, non-perturbative description of the Mott metal-insulator transition. It captures both the local-moment and quasiparticle aspects of correlated electrons, and it predicted the coexistence of Hubbard bands with a coherent quasiparticle peak, which photoemission later confirmed. Combined with density-functional theory, DMFT became the standard quantitative tool for transition-metal oxides, actinides, iron pnictides, nickelates and Hund's metals, and it explained phenomena that band theory cannot. Its cluster and diagrammatic extensions underpin modern studies of high-temperature superconductivity. Over three decades DMFT has changed how physicists compute and understand quantum materials.
